title: Physics-tailored machine learning reveals unexpected non-reciprocal forces in dusty plasmas
summary: A neural network built with physical constraints was trained on 3D particle-tracking data from a laboratory dusty plasma to infer the interaction forces between particles. The method describes the non-reciprocal forces more precisely than before and shows that some common theoretical assumptions about them are inaccurate. The authors checked their inferred force laws against laboratory experiments, which strengthens the claim, though the result comes from a single experimental system.
ai_technology: Physics-tailored neural network for inferring force laws from particle trajectories

evidence.tested: A physics-constrained neural network fitted to 3D particle-tracking data from a laboratory dusty plasma inferred the interaction forces; particle masses were inferred two independent ways and the force laws were checked against laboratory experiments.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no explicit limitations; the result comes from a single experimental system.
evidence.ai_role: A physics-informed neural network learned the non-reciprocal force laws from tracking data.
